passages.text: Then Moses said to the heads of the tribes of Israel, “This is what the LORD has commanded: If a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath to obligate himself by a pledge, he must not break his word; he must do everything he has promised.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of Israel.
Moses gave them a message from the LORD.
The LORD gave a command.
If a man makes a vow to the LORD, he must keep it.
If a man swears an oath to bind himself by a pledge, he must keep it.
He must not break his word.
He must do everything he has promised.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־ רָאשֵׁ֣י הַמַּטּ֔וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָֽה׃ אִישׁ֩ כִּֽי־ יִדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר לַֽיהוָ֗ה אֽוֹ־ הִשָּׁ֤בַע שְׁבֻעָה֙ לֶאְסֹ֤ר אִסָּר֙ עַל־ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ לֹ֥א יַחֵ֖ל דְּבָר֑וֹ כְּכָל־ הַיֹּצֵ֥א מִפִּ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: And if a woman in her father’s house during her youth makes a vow to the LORD or obligates herself by a pledge, and her father hears about her vow or pledge but says nothing to her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.
passages.sermon:
A young woman may live in her father’s house.
She may make a vow to the LORD.
She may promise to do something and bind herself with a pledge.
Her father may hear about her vow or her pledge.
If her father says nothing to her, he remains silent.
Then her vow will stand.
Every pledge she made to bind herself will stand.
passages.original: וְאִשָּׁ֕ה כִּֽי־ תִדֹּ֥ר נֶ֖דֶר לַיהוָ֑ה וְאָסְרָ֥ה אִסָּ֛ר בְּבֵ֥ית אָבִ֖יהָ בִּנְעֻרֶֽיהָ׃ וְשָׁמַ֨ע אָבִ֜יהָ אֶת־ נִדְרָ֗הּ וֶֽאֱסָרָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽסְרָ֣ה עַל־ נַפְשָׁ֔הּ וְהֶחֱרִ֥ישׁ לָ֖הּ אָבִ֑יהָ וְקָ֙מוּ֙ כָּל־ נְדָרֶ֔יהָ וְכָל־ אִסָּ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־ אָסְרָ֥ה עַל־ נַפְשָׁ֖הּ יָקֽוּם׃

passages.text: But if her father prohibits her on the day he hears about it, then none of the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand. The LORD will absolve her because her father has prohibited her.
passages.sermon:
A young woman may make a vow to the LORD while she lives in her father's house.
Her father may hear about her vow or pledge.
If her father prohibits her on the day he hears about it, her vows will not stand.
None of the pledges by which she has bound herself will remain.
The LORD will forgive her.
Her father has prohibited her.
passages.original: וְאִם־ הֵנִ֨יא אָבִ֣יהָ אֹתָהּ֮ בְּי֣וֹם שָׁמְעוֹ֒ כָּל־ נְדָרֶ֗יהָ וֶֽאֱסָרֶ֛יהָ אֲשֶׁר־ אָסְרָ֥ה עַל־ נַפְשָׁ֖הּ לֹ֣א יָק֑וּם וַֽיהוָה֙ יִֽסְלַח־ לָ֔הּ כִּי־ הֵנִ֥יא אָבִ֖יהָ אֹתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: If a woman marries while under a vow or rash promise by which she has bound herself, and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her on that day, then the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.
passages.sermon:
A woman may make a vow or a promise that binds her.
She may do this before she marries.
She may still be under this vow or promise when she marries.
Her husband may hear about her vow or promise on the day he learns of it.
If her husband says nothing to her on that day, her vow or promise remains in effect.
All the vows or promises she made that bind her will stand.
passages.original: וְאִם־ הָי֤וֹ תִֽהְיֶה֙ לְאִ֔ישׁ וּנְדָרֶ֖יהָ עָלֶ֑יהָ א֚וֹ מִבְטָ֣א שְׂפָתֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָסְרָ֖ה עַל־ נַפְשָֽׁהּ׃ וְשָׁמַ֥ע אִישָׁ֛הּ בְּי֥וֹם שָׁמְע֖וֹ וְהֶחֱרִ֣ישׁ לָ֑הּ וְקָ֣מוּ נְדָרֶ֗יהָ וֶֽאֱסָרֶ֛הָ אֲשֶׁר־ אָסְרָ֥ה עַל־ נַפְשָׁ֖הּ יָקֻֽמוּ׃

passages.text: But if her husband prohibits her when he hears of it, he nullifies the vow that binds her or the rash promise she has made, and the LORD will absolve her.
passages.sermon:
A married woman may make a vow or a promise that binds her.
Her husband may hear about her vow or promise.
If her husband hears about it, he can act immediately.
If her husband prohibits her on the day he hears, he nullifies her vow.
He also nullifies any promise she made to bind herself.
Her vow or promise does not stand.
The LORD forgives her.
The LORD forgives her because her husband prohibited her.
passages.original: וְ֠אִם בְּי֨וֹם שְׁמֹ֣עַ אִישָׁהּ֮ יָנִ֣יא אוֹתָהּ֒ וְהֵפֵ֗ר אֶת־ נִדְרָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ וְאֵת֙ מִבְטָ֣א שְׂפָתֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָסְרָ֖ה עַל־ נַפְשָׁ֑הּ וַיהוָ֖ה יִֽסְלַֽח־ לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Every vow a widow or divorced woman pledges to fulfill is binding on her.
passages.sermon:
A widow is a woman whose husband has died.
A divorced woman is a woman whose marriage has ended.
If a widow makes a vow, it is binding on her.
If a divorced woman makes a vow, it is binding on her.
Every promise or obligation she places on herself must stand.
passages.original: וְנֵ֥דֶר אַלְמָנָ֖ה וּגְרוּשָׁ֑ה כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ אָסְרָ֥ה עַל־ נַפְשָׁ֖הּ יָק֥וּם עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: If a woman in her husband’s house has made a vow or put herself under an obligation with an oath, and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her and does not prohibit her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.
passages.sermon:
A married woman may make a vow in her husband's house.
She may also put herself under an obligation with an oath.
Her husband may hear about her vow or oath.
If her husband says nothing to her, he does not stop her.
Then all her vows will stand.
Every obligation she made for herself will remain in effect.
passages.original: וְאִם־ בֵּ֥ית אִישָׁ֖הּ נָדָ֑רָה אֽוֹ־ אָסְרָ֥ה אִסָּ֛ר עַל־ נַפְשָׁ֖הּ בִּשְׁבֻעָֽה׃ וְשָׁמַ֤ע אִישָׁהּ֙ וְהֶחֱרִ֣שׁ לָ֔הּ לֹ֥א הֵנִ֖יא אֹתָ֑הּ וְקָ֙מוּ֙ כָּל־ נְדָרֶ֔יהָ וְכָל־ אִסָּ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־ אָסְרָ֥ה עַל־ נַפְשָׁ֖הּ יָקֽוּם׃

passages.text: But if her husband nullifies them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether her vows or pledges, shall stand. Her husband has nullified them, and the LORD will absolve her.
passages.sermon:
A married woman may make vows or pledges.
Her husband may hear about these vows or pledges.
If her husband nullifies them on the day he hears them, they do not stand.
Nothing she promised with her lips will be binding.
Her husband has canceled her vows and pledges.
The LORD will forgive her.
passages.original: וְאִם־ הָפֵר֩ יָפֵ֨ר אֹתָ֥ם׀ אִישָׁהּ֮ בְּי֣וֹם שָׁמְעוֹ֒ כָּל־ מוֹצָ֨א שְׂפָתֶ֧יהָ לִנְדָרֶ֛יהָ וּלְאִסַּ֥ר נַפְשָׁ֖הּ לֹ֣א יָק֑וּם אִישָׁ֣הּ הֲפֵרָ֔ם וַיהוָ֖ה יִֽסְלַֽח־ לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Her husband may confirm or nullify any vow or any sworn pledge to deny herself.
passages.sermon:
A husband has authority over his wife’s vows.
A husband can confirm any vow his wife makes.
A husband can also nullify any vow his wife makes.
This includes any sworn pledge by which she denies herself.
passages.original: כָּל־ נֵ֛דֶר וְכָל־ שְׁבֻעַ֥ת אִסָּ֖ר לְעַנֹּ֣ת נָ֑פֶשׁ אִישָׁ֥הּ יְקִימֶ֖נּוּ וְאִישָׁ֥הּ יְפֵרֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: But if her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he confirms all the vows and pledges that bind her. He has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard about them.
passages.sermon:
A husband can confirm or nullify his wife's vows and pledges.
If a husband hears his wife's vows or pledges, he must respond.
If the husband says nothing to his wife from day to day, he confirms her vows and pledges.
He confirms all the vows and all the pledges that bind her.
He confirms them because he remained silent on the day he heard about them.
passages.original: וְאִם־ הַחֲרֵשׁ֩ יַחֲרִ֨ישׁ לָ֥הּ אִישָׁהּ֮ מִיּ֣וֹם אֶל־ יוֹם֒ וְהֵקִים֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ נְדָרֶ֔יהָ א֥וֹ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֱסָרֶ֖יהָ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלֶ֑יהָ הֵקִ֣ים אֹתָ֔ם כִּי־ הֶחֱרִ֥שׁ לָ֖הּ בְּי֥וֹם שָׁמְעֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But if he nullifies them after he hears of them, then he will bear her iniquity.”
passages.sermon: A husband can hear his wife's vows or pledges.\r\nIf the husband cancels these vows or pledges after he hears them,\r\nthen the husband will carry the responsibility for her wrongdoing.
passages.original: וְאִם־ הָפֵ֥ר יָפֵ֛ר אֹתָ֖ם אַחֲרֵ֣י שָׁמְע֑וֹ וְנָשָׂ֖א אֶת־ עֲוֺנָֽהּ׃

passages.text: These are the statutes that the LORD commanded Moses concerning the relationship between a man and his wife, and between a father and a young daughter still in his home.
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave commands to Moses.
These commands are statutes.
The statutes concern relationships in the family.
They concern a man and his wife.
They also concern a father and his young daughter.
The statutes apply when the daughter still lives in her father's house.
passages.original: אֵ֣לֶּה הַֽחֻקִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֵּ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ לְאִשְׁתּ֑וֹ בֵּֽין־ אָ֣ב לְבִתּ֔וֹ בִּנְעֻרֶ֖יהָ בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיהָ׃פ
